headline: Acquisitions accelerate. Budgets expand. Delays persist.
deck: This week, companies are consolidating while budgets for space resilience grow, but some tests still can't seem to get off the ground.

stories.head: Intuitive Machines buys ground station for lunar Wi-Fi
stories.body: Intuitive Machines is acquiring a ground station company to enhance its lunar communications network, emphasizing the importance of connectivity in space. This move comes amid their ongoing lunar mission preparations, reinforcing that even lunar landers need reliable Wi-Fi. The financial details remain undisclosed, but it signals a strategic pivot towards robust communication infrastructure.
stories.soWhat: With lunar missions on the rise, expect more companies to prioritize ground infrastructure—because even space needs solid customer support.

stories.head: Golden Dome chief defends $1.2 trillion interceptor plan
stories.body: Gen. Michael Guetlein is pushing back against the Congressional Budget Office's $1.2 trillion estimate for his space interceptor plans, arguing that affordability is the real challenge in the space race. This public defense highlights the ongoing tension between ambitious defense projects and fiscal realities, as military budgets face scrutiny. The stakes are high, and the clock is ticking.
stories.soWhat: This isn’t just about numbers; it’s a reminder that the real battle is convincing Congress to fund your vision amidst rising costs.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has successfully raised $190 million in a Series C round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This funding round signals strong interest in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, areas that are increasingly relevant as geopolitical tensions rise. The DoD's interest in their technology is a clear endorsement of their mission.
stories.soWhat: In a world of space threats, investors are betting big on security solutions—because who doesn’t want a safety net in orbit?

watchlist.title: Monitor AST SpaceMobile's Vulcan launch plans
watchlist.body: If AST SpaceMobile partners with ULA for launches, it could reshape their satellite deployment strategy and impact market dynamics.

watchlist.title: Watch for hypersonic test delays
watchlist.body: The continued slips in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests could further erode confidence in defense timelines and budgets.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension implications
watchlist.body: With a $480 million extension on the TITAN program, Palantir's role in defense logistics could expand significantly.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Sierra Space's Dream Chaser
watchlist.body: Following its critical design review pass, the next steps for Sierra Space will be crucial in determining its future in the DoD market.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
